text: If you dug a hole straight through the Earth and jumped in, you'd pop out the other side in about thirty-eight minutes... and then fall right back in.
First, you'd have to dig through almost thirteen thousand kilometres of rock.
The deepest hole humans have ever dug only reached about twelve kilometres. Today it's just a small rusty cap in the ground.
Below the crust is the mantle: hot rock that slowly flows, like incredibly thick toffee.
Then the outer core, an ocean of liquid metal, and finally the inner core, about as hot as the surface of the Sun.
But let's say you had a magic, heat-proof tube, with all the air sucked out. You jump.
Gravity pulls you faster and faster. By the centre, you're moving about as fast as a rocket heading into orbit.
And right at the centre, you'd feel completely weightless, because the whole planet is pulling you equally in every direction.
Then you start slowing down, rising up towards the other side, until you pop out, about thirty-eight minutes after you jumped.
But here's the crazy part. Unless someone grabs you, you'd fall straight back down and do it all again... forever. A human yo-yo.
And if you jumped in from the UK, you'd pop out in the Pacific Ocean, near New Zealand.
So... would you jump? Tell me in the comments.
